rationale: Both independently rediscover the GitHub-vs-MkDocs image path issue with equal rigor and precision. But X goes substantially further: it critiques the newly-added 'Live Runner State and Ownership' section as overstating the single-consumer connector-drain guarantee (citing three other drain call sites), surfaces a plausible TP>1 collective hazard, validates the prefix-cache note and full-payload-unreachability fix, and flags a YAML/doc inconsistency — covering far more of the ground-truth concern space (platform scope, connector ownership, full-payload branch, prefix cache) with concrete file:line actionability. Y's single finding is solid but leaves most of the ground-truth thread (deeper connector-ownership nuance, prefix cache, SVG labeling) untouched, giving it much lower recall despite comparable per-finding precision.
